info.title: WikiWatch API
info.description: Instructor-provided backend for frontend training. One shared team. Real database, role permissions, review transitions and plain-text diff comments. Public Wikimedia reads stay in the browser. Login, copy access_token, then use Authorize. All JSON success responses use {success, data}.

post.summary: Log in with email and password

post.description: Each refresh token can be used once. Old access token is revoked too. Serialize refresh requests in the frontend.

get.summary: Read the current account and role

post.summary: Admit a bounded batch of stream edits to the shared queue
post.description: Reviewer or lead. Metadata supplied by the client is not independently verified. Same wiki/new_rev is idempotent. Do not submit the complete global firehose. Max 100 per request; queue is capped.

get.summary: Read the shared queue or a status column
get.description: All signed-in roles. Filters are applied on the server. My Claims uses owner_id from /auth/me. These are admitted team edits, not all Wikipedia edits.

get.summary: Read one edit and its current version

post.summary: Claim, review, assign, verify, return, release, or reopen
post.description: Reviewer: claim unclaimed; OK/flag/release own claimed or returned edit. Lead: assign unfinished edits; release claimed; return/verify flagged; reopen completed. Flags and returns need a reason. Version is required. 409 means reload; never show an offline claim as confirmed. A flag does not revert Wikipedia.

get.summary: Read reviewer workload by actual status (lead)
Load persistent threads for one revision pair

post.summary: Start a line or selection comment thread
post.description: Reviewer or lead. Store fixed revision IDs, side, line range, UTF-16 offsets and plain-text quote. No raw HTML. Source lines are not fetched or checked by this API; frontend must detect an anchor mismatch instead of attaching it to different text.

delete.summary: Delete your own thread and hide its replies
delete.description: Soft deletion. Author only. The audit keeps a deletion record. Database rows remain for instructor retention; no other API returns their content.

post.description: Create an account with a password shared separately by the trainer. This does not send an invitation email. No public signup.

patch.description: Cannot remove your own admin access. Unfinished claims must be reassigned or completed before reviewer access is removed.

get.summary: Read names for comment authors and claim owners
get.description: All roles. This directory excludes email addresses and password hashes.

get.summary: Read saved board order and viewed edits

put.summary: Save board order and viewed edits
put.description: Reordering columns changes presentation only. It does not change review states. A stale version returns 409.

get.summary: Catch up on team changes using a durable cursor
get.description: All roles. Poll while the app is visible, with backoff on failures. Events are invalidation signals, not copies of private records. Refetch allowed resources. Keep polling until has_more is false. Cursor 0 starts at the beginning. Realtime transport is REST polling, not a Wikimedia SSE proxy.
Use after_id to export batches of at most 10,000 records. No passwords, tokens, or comment bodies are included in audit details.

200.description: CSV download, with spreadsheet formula protection

get.description: Counts only edits admitted to the shared queue, including archived edits. This is not the global Wikimedia edit rate or a measured revert rate. Missing minutes have zero observations. Frontend fills those chart bins.

start_offset.title: Start Offset
start_offset.description: UTF-16 offset within the plain-text line, as used by JavaScript

source_hash.title: Source Hash
source_hash.description: Optional hash of the full plain-text revision, for frontend stale-anchor detection

quote.title: Quote
quote.description: Plain text only. Never store DOM or diff HTML.
